metadata.title: Six Standard Deviations Suffice
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Discrepancy of a set
nodes.statement: Given a two-coloring (Red/Blue) of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the discrepancy $\mathrm{disc}(X)$ of a set $X \subset \{1,\ldots,n\}$ is the number of Red points in $X$ minus the number of Blue points in $X$.
nodes.statement_clean: Discrepancy of a set under a two-coloring: count of one color minus count of the other.

nodes.name: Rudin-Shapiro function
nodes.statement: A Rudin-Shapiro function (with respect to $K$) is a polynomial $f(z) = \epsilon_1 z + \cdots + \epsilon_n z^n$ with $\epsilon_i \in \{-1,+1\}$ such that $\|f\| = \max_{|z|=1}|f(z)| \le K\sqrt{n}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Polynomial with $\pm 1$ coefficients whose sup-norm on the unit circle is bounded by $K\sqrt{n}$.

nodes.name: Hamming diameter
nodes.statement: For a set $\mathcal{A} \subset \{-1,+1\}^r$, $\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{A})$ is the maximum Hamming distance between two elements of $\mathcal{A}$, where the Hamming metric $\rho$ counts coordinates where two vectors differ.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximum Hamming distance between two elements of a subset of the discrete cube.

nodes.name: Entropy function
nodes.statement: $H(\alpha) = -\alpha \log_2 \alpha - (1-\alpha)\log_2(1-\alpha)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Binary entropy function.

nodes.name: Subgaussian tail bound for Rademacher sums
nodes.statement: For $X = \epsilon_1 a_1 + \cdots + \epsilon_n a_n$ with $\epsilon_i$ uniform $\pm 1$ and $\sigma^2 = a_1^2 + \cdots + a_n^2$: $\Pr[|X| > \lambda \sigma] < 2 e^{-\lambda^2/2}$ for all $\lambda > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Hoeffding/Chernoff-type tail inequality for a Rademacher sum.
nodes.origin_citation: Spencer, Compositio Math. 47 (1982); standard Hoeffding bound

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (Main: linear forms)
nodes.statement: Let $L_i(x_1,\ldots,x_n) = a_{i1}x_1 + \cdots + a_{in}x_n$, $1 \le i \le n$, with all $|a_{ij}| \le 1$. Then there exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n \in \{-1,+1\}$ such that $|L_i(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n)| \le K\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$, where $K$ is an absolute constant.
nodes.statement_clean: For $n$ linear forms in $n$ variables with bounded coefficients, there exists a $\pm 1$ assignment making each form bounded by $K\sqrt{n}$.
conclusions: There exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n \in \{-1,+1\}$ with $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le K\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$

nodes.name: Corollary 2 (Set discrepancy on $n$ elements)
nodes.statement: Let $A_1,\ldots,A_n \subset \{1,\ldots,n\}$. Then there exists a two-coloring of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that $|\mathrm{disc}(A_i)| \le K\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Any $n$ subsets of an $n$-element set admit a two-coloring with all discrepancies $O(\sqrt{n})$.
conclusions: Two-coloring exists with $|\mathrm{disc}(A_i)| \le K\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$

nodes.name: Theorem 3 (Discrepancy for arbitrary finite sets)
nodes.statement: Let $A_1,\ldots,A_n \subset \Omega$ be arbitrary finite sets, $\Omega$ finite of arbitrary size. Then there exists a two-coloring of $\Omega$ such that $|\mathrm{disc}(A_i)| \le K\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$. This resolves a question of Paul Erdős.
nodes.statement_clean: Extends Corollary 2 by removing the $|\Omega|=n$ restriction.
conclusions: There exists a two-coloring of $\Omega$ with $|\mathrm{disc}(A_i)| \le K\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$

nodes.name: Lemma 4 (Basic existence with zero coordinates)
nodes.statement: Given $n$ linear forms in $n$ variables with $|a_{ij}| \le 1$, for $n$ sufficiently large there exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n \in \{-1,0,+1\}$ with $|\{i: \epsilon_i = 0\}| \le 4 \times 10^{-10} n$ and $|L_i(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n)| \le K\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Three-valued $\{-1,0,+1\}$ assignment with few zeros and small forms; the basic ingredient combining the probabilistic method with pigeonhole.

nodes.name: Theorem 5 (Kleitman's diameter bound)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A} \subset \{-1,+1\}^r$, $s \le r/2$, $|\mathcal{A}| > \sum_{i=0}^{s-1} \binom{r}{i}$. Then $\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{A}) \ge 2s$. Equivalently, if $|\mathcal{A}| > 2^{r H(1/2 - p)}$ with $p > 0$ then $\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{A}) \ge (1-2p) r$.
nodes.statement_clean: Kleitman's isodiametric inequality: any large enough subset of the discrete cube must contain two points far apart in Hamming distance.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Define a roundoff map $T: \{-1,+1\}^n \to \mathbb{Z}^n$, identify a small `bad-region' $B \subset \mathbb{Z}^n$, show $|T^{-1}(B)| \ge \frac{1}{2} 2^n$ (probabilistic) and $|B| \le 2^{cn}$ (counting via entropy), then apply pigeonhole and Kleitman to extract two cube-vectors at large Hamming distance whose half-difference gives the desired $\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Define roundoff $T$ and target set $B$
nodes.statement: Define $T: \{-1,+1\}^n \to \mathbb{Z}^n$ by $T(\epsilon) = (b_1,\ldots,b_n)$ where $b_i$ is the nearest integer to $L_i(\epsilon)/(20\sqrt{n})$. Define $B \subset \mathbb{Z}^n$ by tail-control conditions: $|\{i:|b_i| \ge s\}| \le n(2 e^{-(2s-1)^2 \cdot 50}) \cdot 2^{s+1}$ for all $s \ge 1$.

nodes.name: Probabilistic lower bound on $|T^{-1}(B)|$
nodes.statement: Using $\Pr[|L_i| \ge \lambda \sqrt{n}] \le 2 e^{-\lambda^2/2}$ and Markov, show each tail-condition fails with probability $\le 1/2^{s+1}$, summing to $\Pr[T(\epsilon) \notin B] \le 1/2$, hence $|T^{-1}(B)| \ge \frac{1}{2} 2^n$.

nodes.name: Counting upper bound on $|B|$
nodes.statement: Bound $|B| \le 2^{cn}$ with $c = \sum_s [H(\alpha_s) + \alpha_s] \sim H(8 e^{-50}) < 1.1 \times 10^{-19}$ via crude entropy counting.

nodes.name: Pigeonhole + Kleitman to extract $\mathcal{A}$
nodes.statement: By pigeonhole pick $b \in B$ with $\mathcal{A} = T^{-1}(b)$ satisfying $|\mathcal{A}| \ge 2^{n(1-c)-1} > 2^{n H(1/2-p)}$. Apply Theorem 5 to get $\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{A}) \ge (1-2p)n$ with $p \sim 2 \times 10^{-10}$.

nodes.name: Form $\epsilon = (\epsilon' - \epsilon'')/2$
nodes.statement: Pick $\epsilon', \epsilon'' \in \mathcal{A}$ at maximum Hamming distance. Set $\epsilon = (\epsilon' - \epsilon'')/2 \in \{-1,0,+1\}^n$. Since $T(\epsilon') = T(\epsilon'')$, $L_i(\epsilon')$ and $L_i(\epsilon'')$ lie in a common interval of length $20\sqrt{n}$, so $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le 10\sqrt{n}$, and the number of zero coordinates is $n - \mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{A}) \le 2pn$.

nodes.name: Lemma 6 (Generalized $r$-variable version)
nodes.statement: Let $r \le n$ and $L_i(x_1,\ldots,x_r) = a_{i1} x_1 + \cdots + a_{ir} x_r$, $1 \le i \le n$, with $|a_{ij}| \le 1$. For $r$ sufficiently large there exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_r \in \{-1,0,+1\}$ with $|\{i:\epsilon_i=0\}| \le c r$, $c = 6 \times 10^{-7}$, and $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le 10 \sqrt{r} \sqrt{\ln(2 n/r)}$ for $1 \le i \le n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalization of Lemma 4 to $r \le n$ variables with an extra $\sqrt{\ln(2n/r)}$ factor.

nodes.name: Theorem 7 (Linear forms, $r$ variables)
nodes.statement: Let $r \le n$ and $L_i(x_1,\ldots,x_r) = \sum_j a_{ij} x_j$, $1 \le i \le n$, with $|a_{ij}| \le 1$. For $r$ sufficiently large there exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_r \in \{-1,+1\}$ with $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le 11 \sqrt{r}\sqrt{\ln(2n/r)}$ for $1 \le i \le n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Iterating Lemma 6 yields a pure $\pm 1$ solution; Theorem 1 follows by setting $r = n$, giving $K = 11\sqrt{\ln 2} < 9.2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7
nodes.statement: Iterate Lemma 6: start with $r = r_0$ variables, apply Lemma 6 to fix all but $r_1 \le c r_0$ variables, repeat to get $r_0 > r_1 > \cdots > r_{u+1}$ with $r_{u+1} < k$. Sum the contributions: $|L_i| \le k + \sum_{j} 10 \sqrt{r c^j} \sqrt{\ln(2n/(rc^j))} \le k + 10.05 \sqrt{r}\sqrt{\ln(2n/r)}$ via $\sum c^{-j/2}$ geometric bound. For large $r$ the constant $k$ is absorbed.

nodes.name: Probabilistic method via Hadamard matrices
nodes.statement: Existence proofs leave open finding an explicit $A$ with $|\mathcal{A}_A|$ exponentially small. The author conjectures that Hadamard matrices yield such $A$, with strong evidence but no proof.

nodes.name: Corollary 8 (Approximation of fractional initial values)
nodes.statement: Let $L_i(x) = \sum_j a_{ij} x_j$, $1 \le i \le n$, $|a_{ij}| \le 1$, and $p_1,\ldots,p_n \in [0,1]$. Then there exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n \in \{0,1\}$ such that $|L_i(\epsilon) - L_i(p)| \le K\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$, with the same constant $K$ as Theorem 1.
nodes.statement_clean: Round real-valued initial conditions $p_j \in [0,1]$ to $\{0,1\}$ while preserving each linear form within $K\sqrt{n}$.
conclusions: There exist $\epsilon_j \in \{0,1\}$ with $|L_i(\epsilon) - L_i(p)| \le K\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$

nodes.name: Theorem 9 (Reduction to $n$ variables)
nodes.statement: Let $L_i(x_1,\ldots,x_r) = \sum_j a_{ij} x_j$, $1 \le i \le n$, with $r \ge n$. Then there exist $x_1,\ldots,x_r \in [-1,+1]$ with $L_i(x) = 0$ for all $i$ and $|\{j : x_j \notin \{-1,+1\}\}| \le n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Underdetermined linear systems admit a $\pm 1$ solution on all but at most $n$ coordinates.

nodes.name: Theorem 10 (Linear forms, $r > n$ variables)
nodes.statement: Let $r \ge n$ and $L_i(x_1,\ldots,x_r) = \sum_j a_{ij} x_j$, $1 \le i \le n$, $|a_{ij}| \le 1$. Then there exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_r \in \{-1,+1\}$ with $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le 2 K \sqrt{n}$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Linear-forms bound when there are more variables than forms; constant doubles compared to Theorem 1.
conclusions: There exist $\epsilon_j \in \{-1,+1\}$ with $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le 2 K \sqrt{n}$ for all $i$

nodes.name: Theorem 11 (Existence of Rudin-Shapiro functions)
nodes.statement: There exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n \in \{-1,+1\}$ such that $f(z) = \sum_{i=1}^n \epsilon_i z^i$ satisfies $\|f\| = \max_{|z|=1}|f(z)| \le K\sqrt{n}$, where $K$ is an absolute constant.
nodes.statement_clean: An alternate proof of the existence of Rudin-Shapiro polynomials.

nodes.name: Theorem 12 (Many low-discrepancy assignments)
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Theorem 1 let $s_K(n)$ denote the number of $\epsilon \in \{-1,+1\}^n$ with $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le K\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$. For all $K \ge K_0$ (an absolute constant), $s_K(n) \ge (2 - \delta_K + o(1))^n$ with $0 < \delta_K < 1$ and $\lim_{K \to \infty} \delta_K = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Exponentially many $\pm 1$ vectors satisfy the Theorem-1 conclusion, almost the full $2^n$.

nodes.name: Corollary 13 (Many Rudin-Shapiro functions)
nodes.statement: There are at least $(2 - \delta_K + o(1))^n$ functions $f(z) = \sum_{i=1}^n \epsilon_i z^i$ with $\|f\| \le K \sqrt{n}$, where $\delta_K$ is as in Theorem 12.
nodes.statement_clean: Rudin-Shapiro functions are exponentially numerous.

nodes.name: Theorem 14 (Bounding the $i$th form)
nodes.statement: Let $L_i(x_1,\ldots,x_n) = \sum_j a_{ij} x_j$, $1 \le i \le m$, $|a_{ij}| \le 1$. Then there exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n \in \{-1,+1\}$ with $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le K\sqrt{i}$ for $1 \le i \le m$.
nodes.statement_clean: The $i$th form's discrepancy can be bounded by $K\sqrt{i}$ (independent of $m$); strengthens an earlier $K\sqrt{i}\,(\ln i)$ result of Beck-Spencer.
conclusions: There exist $\epsilon_j \in \{-1,+1\}$ with $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le K\sqrt{i}$ for $1 \le i \le m$

nodes.name: Lemma 15 (Step lemma for Theorem 14)
nodes.statement: Given $m$ linear forms on $n$ variables with $|a_{ij}| \le 1$, there exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n \in \{-1,0,+1\}$ with $|\{i:\epsilon_i=0\}| \le c n$, $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le K\sqrt{i}/\ln^2(2n/i)$ for $1 \le i \le n$, and $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le K\sqrt{i}/\ln^2(2i/n)$ for $n \le i \le m$, where $K > 0$ and $c < 1$ are absolute constants.
nodes.statement_clean: Lemma analogous to Lemmas 4 and 6, with index-dependent bounds, enabling iteration to Theorem 14.

nodes.name: Lemma 17 (Product bound via log-concavity)
nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon > 0$ and suppose $x_1 + \cdots + x_v \le W$. Then $\prod_{i=1}^v (x_i \epsilon) \le e^{W/e}$ (for $\epsilon = 1$); the general case reduces by setting $y_i = x_i \epsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: Elementary calculus bound used in the entropy estimates of Theorem 16's proof.

nodes.name: Komlos Conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $v_1,\ldots,v_s \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with Euclidean norms $|v_i| \le 1$. János Komlós conjectured that there exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_s \in \{-1,+1\}$ with $\|\epsilon_1 v_1 + \cdots + \epsilon_s v_s\|_\infty \le K$, $K$ an absolute constant for arbitrary $s, n$.
nodes.statement_clean: The Komlos signing problem: bound an $L^\infty$ combination of unit-Euclidean-norm vectors by a constant.

nodes.name: Theorem 16 (Three-valued Komlos)
nodes.statement: Let $v_1,\ldots,v_r \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $|v_i| \le 1$ and $r \le n$. Then there exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_r \in \{-1,0,+1\}$ with $|\{i:\epsilon_i=0\}| \le c r$ and $\|\epsilon_1 v_1 + \cdots + \epsilon_r v_r\|_\infty \le K$, where $c < 1$ and $K$ are positive absolute constants.
nodes.statement_clean: Komlos-type bound with three-valued $\{-1,0,+1\}$ coefficients, only a bounded proportion zero.

nodes.name: Corollary 18 ($K\ln n$ Komlos bound)
nodes.statement: Let $v_1,\ldots,v_r \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $|v_i| \le 1$. Then there exist $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_r \in \{-1,+1\}$ with $\|\epsilon_1 v_1 + \cdots + \epsilon_r v_r\|_\infty \le K'' \ln n$, $K''$ an absolute constant.
nodes.statement_clean: Iterating Theorem 16 yields a $\pm 1$ Komlos signing bounded by $O(\ln n)$.
conclusions: There exist $\epsilon_i \in \{-1,+1\}$ with $\|\sum \epsilon_i v_i\|_\infty \le K'' \ln n$

nodes.name: Theorem 19 (Lower bound: best possible up to constants)
nodes.statement: There exist $a_{ij} \in \{-1,+1\}$, $1 \le i,j \le n$, such that for all $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n \in \{-1,+1\}$ some $|L_i(\epsilon)| \ge k \sqrt{n}(1+o(1))$, where $k$ is an absolute constant.
nodes.statement_clean: Theorem 1's $\sqrt{n}$ bound is tight up to the constant: a Hadamard-like matrix forces some $|L_i| \ge \sqrt{n}$.
conclusions: There exist $a_{ij} \in \{-1,+1\}$ such that $\max_i |L_i(\epsilon)| \ge k\sqrt{n}(1+o(1))$ for every $\epsilon \in \{-1,+1\}^n$

nodes.name: Two proofs of Theorem 19
nodes.statement: Proof 1: counting argument from (3.38) with $k \approx 0.67$ such that $1 - 2\Phi(-k) = 0.5$ shows $|\mathcal{A}_A| < 2^n (0.5)^n = 0$ for some $A$. Proof 2: take $A$ a Hadamard matrix of order $n$; orthogonality gives $\sum_i L_i^2 = n^2$, hence some $|L_i| \ge \sqrt{n}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 20 (CLT-based version of Lemma 6)
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha \le 1$ fixed, and $K$, $\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\ldots$, $\beta$, $p$ satisfy $\beta = \alpha^{-1} \sum_s [H(2\Phi(-K(2s-1))\gamma_s) + 2\Phi(-K(2s-1))\gamma_s]$ with $\sum \gamma_s^{-1} \le 1$ and $H(\frac{1}{2}-p) > 1 - \beta$. Then for $n$ large enough, given $n$ linear forms in $r \le \alpha n$ variables with $|a_{ij}| \le 1$ there exist $\epsilon_i \in \{-1,0,+1\}$ with $|\{i:\epsilon_i=0\}| \le 2 p (\alpha n)$ and $|L_i(\epsilon)| \le K\sqrt{r}$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sharper CLT-based version of Lemma 6 using $\Phi(-k)$ in place of $\exp(-k^2/2)$, used to push $K$ down to 5.32.

nodes.name: Calculation: $K \le 5.32$ via tradeoffs
nodes.statement: Bound $G(\alpha)$ recursively via $G(\alpha) \le K\sqrt{\alpha} + G(2 p \alpha)$ from Lemma 20 and $G(\alpha) \le 11\sqrt{\alpha^{-1} \ln(2\alpha^{-1})}$ from Theorem 7. Three steps with $K=4,5,6$ at $\alpha = 1, 0.04, 0.001$ followed by Theorem 7 at $\alpha = 10^{-5}$ give $G(1) \le 4 + 1 + 0.19 + 0.13 = 5.32$.
nodes.statement_clean: Numerical optimization yielding the title's bound $K \le 6$, in fact $K \le 5.32$.

nodes.name: No polynomial-time algorithm known
nodes.statement: The author has not found a polynomial-time algorithm to produce the $\epsilon$ of Lemma 4 or its derivatives; the obstacle is the use of the pigeonhole principle.

nodes.name: Relation to Beck-Fiala bound
nodes.statement: The Komlos Conjecture, applied to incidence column vectors of a set system in which every point lies in at most $d$ sets, would yield a two-coloring with $\mathrm{disc}(A_i) \le K\sqrt{d}$, improving the Beck-Fiala bound $\mathrm{disc}(A_i) \le 2d - 1$.
